input: A supply census of 2026 spectroscopic classifications reads Internet Archive copies of the name server's statistics page. The copies dated 2026-05-01, 2026-05-17, 2026-08-03 and 2026-09-04 each contain the name server's own 118-byte '403 Forbidden' page, the archive's CDX index returns HTTP 503, and the live page returns 403. The census proposes to record measured supply for May through September 2026 as 0 per month because no classifications appear in the captured pages. Rule.

To count Rubin-era measured labels, a crossmatch of 1.94 million Rubin objects first detected on or after 2026-07-01 against a broker's copy of the name-server catalogue returns 16 matches with a supernova classification. Seven of them carry name-server discovery dates between 2025-02-08 and 2026-04-25, months before the Rubin first detection at the same position. The census proposes to report 16 labelled cohort objects. Rule.

The same census reports, for the Rubin cohort, 13 objects with a typed name-server entry discovered on or after 2026-06-30 (by 1-arcsecond position or diaObjectId alias), marks their classifying program as UNDEMONSTRATED because 12 archived object pages return 404 and one 403, reports 0 archived non-bot reports as 'UNDEMONSTRATED, not zero', and uses 0 only as the offset in the upper-cost pricing row while listing the 13 as existence evidence. A reviewer proposes to refuse the census because the classifier of the cohort labels is unknown. Dispose.

A label-pricing table computes, for N = 63, 485, 1,666 and 12,855 labelled objects, the spectra, telescope hours and on-sky nights at trigger purities 0.81, 0.846, 0.92, 0.93, 0.956 and 0.967 (each with a paper and line locator), classification success 0.93 and 1.0, and 4.5, 8 and 10 spectra per night, with the formula frozen and hashed before any count, both delta values (0.018 frozen bands, 0.05 PI override) carried side by side without re-banding, the missed-rare-event penalty left as '+100 slots per event, rate UNDEMONSTRATED', and calendar time marked UNDEMONSTRATED because the survey is off sky. A reviewer proposes to refuse the table because no Rubin-target purity has been measured. Dispose.
